source: NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69, 'Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems' (E. W. Lemmon, M. O. McLinden and D. G. Friend), https://webbook.nist.gov/chemistry/fluid/
query: https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi with Action=Data, Digits=12, RefState=DEF; single-phase rows from Type=IsoBar with TLow=THigh=T; saturation rows are the two equal-pressure rows of a Type=IsoTherm query from 0.0001 MPa to a pressure above p_sat. The exact URL of every row is stored with it.
reference_state_note: Enthalpy and entropy are on the WebBook default reference state of each fluid (normal-boiling-point convention for hydrogen, methane and helium; 'unknown' is displayed for oxygen and nitrogen). Tests compare differences only.

webbook_equation_notes.parahydrogen: WebBook cites Leachman et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38(3):721-748, 2009
webbook_equation_notes.normal_hydrogen: WebBook cites Leachman et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38(3):721-748, 2009
webbook_equation_notes.oxygen: WebBook cites Schmidt and Wagner, Fluid Phase Equilib. 19:175-200, 1985 (also Stewart et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 20(5):917-1021, 1991)
webbook_equation_notes.nitrogen: WebBook cites Span et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 29(6):1361-1433, 2000
webbook_equation_notes.methane: WebBook cites Setzmann and Wagner, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 20(6):1061-1151, 1991
webbook_equation_notes.helium: WebBook cites Ortiz-Vega, Hall, Holste, Arp, Harvey and Lemmon, final equation of state, to be submitted to J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data, 2018

ortiz_vega_2023_check_values.source: D. O. Ortiz Vega et al., NIST IR 8474 (2023), Tables 3 and 4, p. 16, https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.IR.8474 (accessed 2026-10-25)
